Annex VI outlines the conformity assessment procedure based on internal control, requiring providers to verify quality management system compliance with Article 17, examine technical documentation against essential requirements in Chapter III Section 2, and ensure consistency between design/development, post-market monitoring (Article 72), and technical documentation. Annex VII describes conformity assessment based on evaluating both the quality management system and technical documentation. It details application requirements including provider details, list of covered AI systems, technical documentation, QMS documentation, procedures to maintain adequacy, and a declaration of non-duplication. The notified body assesses the QMS against Article 17, notifies the provider with reasoned decisions, and maintains surveillance. Providers must continuously implement the approved system and notify the notified body of any intended changes, which are examined to determine if reassessment is needed.

nodes.title: ANNEX VII  Conformity based on an assessment of the quality management system and an assessment of the technical documentation
nodes.summary: This text from EU Regulation 2024/1689 covers Annexes VII and VIII. Annex VII details the conformity assessment procedure based on quality management system (QMS) and technical documentation assessment. It specifies: (1) application requirements for QMS approval including provider details, AI systems list, technical documentation, and declarations; (2) notified body assessment procedures and decision notifications; (3) handling of QMS changes; (4) technical documentation control, including notified body access to training/validation/testing datasets, models, and parameters (subject to IP protections), issuance or refusal of Union technical documentation assessment certificates, retraining requirements for non-compliant data, and handling of AI system changes; (5) surveillance through periodic audits and premises access. Annex VIII lists registration information required under Article 49 for high-risk AI systems, including provider/representative details, trade name, intended purpose, operating logic, system status, certificate details, Member States of availability, EU declaration of conformity, and electronic instructions (with exceptions for law enforcement/migration systems).

nodes.title: ANNEX VIII  Information to be submitted upon the registration of high-risk AI systems in accordance with Article 49
nodes.summary: This text contains Annexes VIII and IX of EU Regulation 2024/1689 (AI Act). Annex VIII details registration information required for high-risk AI systems under Article 49, divided into three sections: Section A lists information providers must submit for Article 49(1) registrations, including provider/representative contact details, AI system identification, intended purpose, operating logic, status, notified body certificates, Member States of deployment, EU declaration of conformity, and electronic instructions. Section B covers Article 49(2) registrations for systems deemed non-high-risk under Article 6(3), requiring similar provider details and justification. Section C specifies information deployers must submit under Article 49(3), including deployer contacts, EU database URL, and summaries of fundamental rights and data protection impact assessments. Annex IX outlines information required for registering real-world testing of high-risk AI systems under Article 60, including a unique identification number, provider/deployer details, system description, testing plan characteristics, and suspension/termination information.

nodes.title: ANNEX IX  Information to be submitted upon the registration of high-risk AI systems listed in AnnexIII in relation to testing in real world conditions in accordance with Article 60
nodes.summary: This text contains two annexes from EU Regulation 2024/1689 (AI Act). Annex IX specifies the information required for registering high-risk AI systems (listed in Annex III) undergoing real-world testing under Article 60, including: a Union-wide unique identification number; names and contact details of providers and deployers; a description of the AI system and its intended purpose; a summary of the testing plan; and information on any suspension or termination of testing. Annex X lists Union legislative acts on large-scale IT systems in the area of Freedom, Security and Justice, covering: (1) the Schengen Information System (Regulations 2018/1860, 2018/1861, 2018/1862); (2) the Visa Information System (Regulations 2021/1133 and 2021/1134); (3) Eurodac (Regulation 2024/1358); and (4) the Entry/Exit System (Regulation 2017/2226), providing full citations for each legislative act.

nodes.title: ANNEX X  Union legislative acts on large-scale IT systems in the area of Freedom, Security and Justice
nodes.summary: This text contains two annexes from EU Regulation 2024/1689. Annex X lists Union legislative acts on large-scale IT systems in the area of Freedom, Security and Justice, covering: (1) Schengen Information System (Regulations 2018/1860, 2018/1861, 2018/1862); (2) Visa Information System (Regulations 2021/1133, 2021/1134); (3) Eurodac (Regulation 2024/1358); (4) Entry/Exit System (Regulation 2017/2226); (5) European Travel Information and Authorisation System/ETIAS (Regulations 2018/1240, 2018/1241); (6) ECRIS-TCN for third-country nationals (Regulation 2019/816); and (7) Interoperability frameworks (Regulations 2019/817, 2019/818). Annex XI specifies technical documentation requirements for providers of general-purpose AI models under Article 53(1)(a). Section 1 requires all providers to document: general model description (tasks, use policies, release date, architecture, parameters, modality, licence) and detailed development elements (technical integration means, design specifications, training data details, computational resources, energy consumption). Section 2 requires providers of models with systemic risk to additionally provide detailed evaluation strategies including criteria, metrics, methodology, and results.

nodes.title: ANNEX XI  Technical documentation referred to in Article 53(1), point(a) — technical documentation for providers of general-purpose AI models
nodes.summary: This text presents Annexes XI and XII of EU Regulation 2024/1689, specifying technical documentation requirements for providers of general-purpose AI models under Article 53(1). Annex XI, Section 1 lists information all providers must supply: general model description (tasks, use policies, release date, architecture, parameters, modality, licence), development details (technical integration means, design specifications, training data and methodologies, computational resources, energy consumption). Section 2 adds requirements for providers of models with systemic risk: evaluation strategies and results, adversarial testing measures (e.g., red teaming), alignment/fine-tuning, and system architecture description. Annex XII outlines transparency information providers must share with downstream providers integrating the model into AI systems, including general model description (tasks, policies, distribution, hardware/software interactions, software versions, architecture, modality, licence) and development elements (integration means, input/output modalities and maximum size, training/testing/validation data provenance and curation).

nodes.title: ANNEX XII  Transparency information referred to in Article 53(1), point(b) — technical documentation for providers of general-purpose AI models to downstream providers that integrate the model into their AI system
nodes.summary: This text contains two annexes from EU Regulation 2024/1689 on AI. Annex XII specifies transparency information and technical documentation that providers of general-purpose AI models must give to downstream providers integrating the model into their AI systems. This includes a general model description (intended tasks, acceptable use policies, release date, distribution methods, hardware/software interactions, software versions, architecture, parameters, input/output modality and format, licence) and details on model elements and development process (technical means for integration, input/output modalities and maximum size, and information on training, testing and validation data including type, provenance, and curation methodologies). Annex XIII outlines criteria the Commission uses to designate general-purpose AI models with systemic risk under Article 51, including: number of parameters, dataset quality/size, training computation (FLOPs, cost, time, energy), input/output modalities and state-of-the-art thresholds, capability benchmarks and evaluations (autonomy, scalability, tools), internal market impact (presumed at 10,000+ EU business users), and number of registered end-users.

nodes.title: ANNEX XIII  Criteria for the designation of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk referred to in Article 51
nodes.summary: This text contains two annexes from EU Regulation 2024/1689 (AI Act). Annex XIII lists criteria for designating general-purpose AI models with systemic risk under Article 51, including: number of model parameters; quality/size of dataset (e.g., tokens); training computation (FLOPs, cost, time, energy); input/output modalities and state-of-the-art thresholds; benchmarks and capability evaluations (task count, adaptability, autonomy, scalability, tool access); high market impact (presumed at 10,000+ registered EU business users); and number of registered end-users. Annex XIV establishes codes, categories, and AI system types for the notification procedure under Article 30, defining the scope of designation for notified conformity assessment bodies. It lists codes AIP 0102–0112 for AI systems under Annex I Section A points 2–12; codes AIB 0201–0203 for Annex III point 1 systems (remote biometric identification, biometric categorisation, emotion recognition); and AI technology-specific code AIH 0101 for symbolic AI, expert/knowledge-based systems, and search/optimisation-based AI.

nodes.title: ANNEX XIV
nodes.summary: This text presents Annex XIV of Regulation 2024/1689 (as amended by M1), which lists codes, categories, and corresponding types of AI systems for the notification procedure under Article 30, defining the scope of designation for notified conformity assessment bodies. It explains that only designated bodies may conduct conformity assessments for high-risk AI systems. The annex provides: (a) AIP codes 0102–0112 for AI systems under Annex I Section A points 2–12; (b) AIB codes 0201–0203 for Annex III point 1 systems (remote biometric identification, biometric categorisation, emotion recognition); and AI technology-specific codes including AIH 0101 (symbolic AI/expert systems), AIH 0201–0205 (machine learning categories by data type: structured, signal/audio, text, image/video, environmental learning), AIH 0301 (generative AI and general-purpose AI models), and AIH 0401 (emerging technologies including Agentic AI). Conformity assessment bodies must use these codes when applying for designation under Article 29.

summary: EU Regulation 2024/1689 (AI Act), adopted 13 June 2024, establishes harmonised rules on artificial intelligence. Chapter I sets general provisions, scope, definitions, AI literacy, and limited processing of special data for bias correction. Chapter II prohibits manipulative, exploitative, social scoring, predictive policing, untargeted scraping, emotion inference, biometric categorisation, and real-time biometric identification practices, with narrow law-enforcement exceptions. Chapter III classifies and regulates high-risk AI, setting requirements (risk management, data governance, documentation, oversight, accuracy), operator obligations, notified bodies, conformity assessment, CE marking, and EU database registration. Chapter IV imposes transparency duties for AI interactions, generative content, emotion/biometric systems, and deepfakes. Chapter V governs general-purpose AI models, including systemic-risk classification (10^25 FLOPs threshold), documentation, copyright, codes of practice. Chapter VI supports innovation via sandboxes, real-world testing, SME measures. Chapter VII establishes governance (AI Office, Board, Advisory Forum, Scientific Panel, national authorities). Chapters VIII–IX cover EU database, post-market monitoring, incident reporting, market surveillance, remedies. Chapters X–XIII address codes of conduct, guidelines, delegated acts, committee procedure, penalties (up to €35M/7% turnover), amendments to sectoral legislation, transitional and entry-into-force provisions. Annexes I–XIV list harmonisation legislation, criminal offences, high-risk use cases, technical documentation, conformity assessment procedures, registration data, large-scale IT systems, GPAI documentation and systemic-risk criteria, and notification codes.
